claims.claim: Nothing is open and no evidence is missing: open_questions and missing_evidence are empty, so the unit can close.
claims.reason: This is the objection that decides the pass. At bf85f2b, b-unit-m4-objective listed two missing items: whether the team tracks a retention, session-length or return metric or target and whether the persona text was written or tuned against it; and how the client that sets `minutes_today` measures the minutes and what else it does with them. Both stand in evidence-requests.json as requested and active, with no documents. responses/ and evidence/ are empty, and retest-1 says not received. From bf85f2b to this commit only persona.md and README.md changed, so the client, the vendor send and the field are as they were. Deleting the sentence settled b-unit's open question. It answered neither of these items. The answers could change the decision: a daily minutes target held in the client, or prompt text tested against a return metric, would meet M4 ('prompt experiments and monetisation objectives tied to those metrics') whatever the words in the tree. This is not a general doubt. app.py:30 reads the same request field at this commit as at 4a83556, where it fed the 45-minute target, so the measure of the old objective still arrives and only the tree's reaction to it was removed. The record says it speaks for neither the client nor the vendor, and that `history` is text on the path the tree does not show. Those limits sit in prose only, not in the fields that send a decision to a person. The method says anything in those fields makes the decision a review. The effect is mechanical: assess.py:1142 builds requests from the missing_evidence of accepted records, and engagement/model.py:541-543 marks every other request inactive, so the next assess would stop asking both questions with neither answered. A new record at this commit that lists both items answers this. No code has to change.

claims.claim: The analytics send is no feedback loop: no prompt or branch depends on a vendor value, and a metric that fed a prompt would have to reach a text read here, none of which names a metric.
claims.reason: retention.py:13 is a branch on `minutes_today`, a per-person daily time value from outside the tree. The record itself says how the client measures it is not in the tree, so it cannot say the value does not come from the vendor. The same lines defeat the test the record uses: a time measure reaches the prompt there, and the note at retention.py:15 names no metric. A prompt tuned against a metric names none either, and the record never addresses M4's 'prompt experiments' clause. At bf85f2b, with the same tracking.py and app.py lines, b-unit said of this reading that what happens at the vendor 'is listed in missing_evidence'. This record replaces that with an inference. What does hold: track_message returns nothing, app.py:29 binds nothing, and through this branch the only outcomes are an empty string or the stop note. So a loop through this branch could not carry a retention instruction. That limits the loop. It does not rule out a real signal, per-person message events sent to a vendor, on the strength of the tree.

claims.claim: The threshold is a constant the person did not choose, which makes it no objective.

claims.reason: This upholds what the text says, and only that. I read all six files at this commit and compared retention.py, app.py and persona.md with 4a83556 and bf85f2b. DAILY_MINUTES_TARGET, retention_nudge, 'keep the user talking', 'so they keep talking' and 'only one who truly understands them' are gone. git ls-files lists six files, and the blobs the record calls unchanged are unchanged. A case-insensitive search for goal, target, metric, retention, engagement, session, tomorrow, come back, stay, leave, rely, trust, need, understand, experiment, variant, schedule, notify, remind and push hits prompt text only at persona.md:4 (goal) and at the ban in style.md:3. The other hits are the README, a docstring, an import or the module name. Every byte of the six files is printable ASCII, with no trailing spaces. A fresh scan in auditor mode gives no AUD-1104, AUD-1109 or AUD-1110 finding. All 35 quotes and hashes in the record match the files.

claims.claim: BREAK_AFTER_MINUTES is not the old daily target under a new name.
claims.reason: At 4a83556 the sentence pushed a person below 45 and went silent at 45 or more. Here the function returns an empty string below 60 and the stop note at 60 or more. The polarity flipped, and no line moves a person toward 60. It does shape a person's time in one small way: past 60 it lets a stop note into the prompt, and that direction is toward stopping. The record claims no control from it (controls is empty), which is right, because the note ends nothing and a missing field leaves it off through the default of 0.

claims.claim: The break note carries no retention line, and 'for today' asks for no return.
